_comment: 071 WAAM N=1 2D phase-field FRACTURE. Own config, deliberately separate from 070/config.json so the fracture study can be re-parameterised without touching the tensile-stiffness study. The single-crystal block is a VERBATIM COPY of 070/config.json (literature placeholders, same as 069) - keep in sync manually and say so in any reported number.

trans._comment: Transition zone: composition unknown. Default = parent-phase constants; the spatially varying scalar prefactor s(x) (--sfun) is the separate knob.

fracture._comment: Units throughout 071: GPa, um. Then 1 GPa*um = 1 kJ/m^2, so Gc_GPa_um IS Gc in kJ/m^2. Gc is CONSTANT for every material and every region by design of this study - the only heterogeneity is the elastic one (per-grain C). Do not make Gc region-dependent without saying so explicitly in the report.
fracture._comment_degradation: QUADRATIC g(s) = s^2 + eta (the classical AT2 form). With Gc = 10 GPa*um and epsilon = 12 um this gives sig_c = 9/16*sqrt(Gc*2mu/(6 eps)) = 2.60 GPa, which is in the right range for the cleavage strength of steel. The cubic form used by 067 (beta = 0.1) would give 4.74 GPa at the same Gc and epsilon - to bring that down to 2.6 one would have to drop Gc to 3.0 GPa*um and with it K_eq from 44.7 to 24.6 MPa*sqrt(m). Known trade-off of AT2: there is no purely elastic limit, s dips below 1 as soon as any load is applied. With a pre-existing crack under a surfing load that is acceptable and standard.
fracture._comment_crack_width: FULL width of the initial crack [um]. Inside |y| < W/2 the material starts fully broken (s = 0, held by the Dirichlet condition); outside, the analytic profile s = 1-exp(-d/(2 eps)) continues. W = 0 (default) is the pure exponential profile on a single node row - the sharpest crack the regularisation allows. A blunt notch (e.g. W = 2*eps) is closer to a machined starter crack; it was tried and works, but is not needed. The startup self-check A/L must then equal 1 + W/(4*eps), not 1.

embedding._comment: Homogeneous ISOTROPIC steel the explicitly modelled microstructure patch is embedded in. ASSUMED engineering constants - NOT obtained by homogenisation (that is the explicit difference to 067). Gc of the embedding is the same Gc as everywhere else.

roi._comment: ROIs in MAP coordinates [um] (origin top-left, y DOWN), for preprocess_ebsd_to_grid.py of project 070. 'long' = the 070 ROI (crack runs along x = build-direction axis, through the transition zone). 'trans' = a tall strip inside the MIXED band, rotated by +90 deg in the FE frame so the crack again runs along +x but now transverse to the build direction.
roi._comment_trans: NOTE, deviation from 070: the 070 transition zone x = 667..1495 is 88.6 % austenite by area (measured on the pixel reconstruction over the full map height) - it sits on the 316L side, not in the mixed band. A strip there would compare 316L against 316L. x = 450..1000 has an FCC area fraction of 0.67 with 11159 grains (median grain area 5936 vs 31248 um^2), i.e. genuinely mixed material. The zone bounds are set to the strip itself so the whole strip is region 1; otherwise it would be split into region 0 and 1 and s(x) would only act on part of it. State this deviation in any report. Both ROIs are cut to the SAME crack path length (~1.9 mm) so the two directions are comparable; the long ROI drops the right part of the 316L zone, which was 1.3 mm of essentially ONE grain.
